Movement in CS2

Movement Mechanics

Mastering movement in CS2 is crucial for survival and effective combat.

Key Principle: Good movement makes you harder to hit while maintaining accuracy.

Basic Movement Techniques

Technique Description Key Binds Difficulty
Counter-strafing Stopping instantly by pressing opposite movement key A/D or W/S Medium
Bunny hop Maintaining momentum through consecutive jumps Space + Strafe High
Air-strafing Controlling movement in air Mouse + A/D High
Remember: Moving while shooting drastically reduces accuracy. Always counter-strafe before shooting!

Advanced Movement Concepts

Silent Landing

Landing without making sound by using crouch.

Execution Hold crouch before landing
Use Case Sneaking behind enemy lines
Fall Height Works up to medium heights

Run Boosting

Boosting teammate by running into them while they jump.

Execution Coordinate jump + forward movement
Use Case Reaching unexpected positions
Players Needed 2 players minimum

Movement Speed Comparison

State Speed (units/s) Sound Level Usage
Running 250 Loud Fast rotations, rushing
Walking 130 Quiet Close combat positioning
Crouching 85 Silent Sneaking, accuracy

Sound System in CS2

Understanding Sound Mechanics

Sound is a crucial information source in CS2, often determining the outcome of rounds.

Key Principle: Every action creates a unique sound that can be used to gain information.

Sound Categories

Type Examples Range Information Provided
Movement Steps, jumps, lands Long Position, direction, player count
Weapons Shots, reloads, scopes Very Long Weapon type, position, ammo status
Utility Pins, bounces, explosions Medium Utility type, timing

Sound-Making Actions

  • Running/Walking
  • Jumping/Landing
  • Weapon switching
  • Reloading
  • Scope zooming
  • Utility usage

Silent Actions

  • Walking with Shift
  • Crouched landing
  • Standing still
  • Looking around
  • Walking on crouch

Sound Masking Techniques

Flash Bang Timing

Using flash explosion to mask movement sounds.

Duration ~1 second of sound cover
Best Used For Position changes, rushes

Fake Steps

Creating misleading sound cues to deceive enemies.

Execution Jump + silent land in different direction
Effectiveness High in clutch situations

Utility Usage

Essential Utility Knowledge

Proper utility usage can turn the tide of any round and is crucial for both execution and defense.

Key Principle: Always have a purpose for your utility and communicate usage with your team.

Utility Mastery Progress

Basic Smokes
Essential for all players
Pop Flashes
Advanced technique
Molotov Lineups
Site specific

Advanced Utility Combinations

Site Execute

1. Flash over for info (avoid blind teammates)

2. Smoke key angles (coordinate timing)

3. Molotov common spots (force movement)

4. Second wave of flashes for entry

Site Hold

1. One-way smokes for advantage

2. Counter-flash common entry points

3. Molotov choke points on push

4. HE stack for heavy damage

Retake Setup

1. Coordinated flashes (multiple angles)

2. Split smokes for map control

3. Molotov plant spot / common angles

4. HE to finish low HP enemies

Position Playing

Understanding Positions

Position selection and playing style can make the difference between winning and losing rounds.

Initial Phase

T Side
  • Default spread positions
  • Early info gathering spots
  • Map control positions
  • Rush setup positions
CT Side
  • Default defensive setup
  • Early aggression spots
  • Utility setup positions
  • Anti-rush positions

Execute Phase

T Side
  • Entry positions
  • Trade setup spots
  • Lurk positions
  • Support positions
CT Side
  • Crossfire positions
  • Rotation spots
  • Flank watch positions
  • Retake setup spots

Post-Plant Phase

T Side
  • After-plant positions
  • Crossfire setups
  • Exit control spots
  • Time management positions
CT Side
  • Retake angles
  • Kit recovery routes
  • Utility usage spots
  • Trade positions

Position Risk Assessment

Off-Angle
High risk, high reward. Best used sparingly and with team support.
Default
Safe but predictable. Good for consistent play and team coordination.
Aggressive
Very high risk. Only use with proper utility and team support.

Economy Management

Economy Basics

Understanding and managing team economy is crucial for maintaining momentum and maximizing round win potential.

Buy Decision Flow

Check Team Money

Evaluate all players' funds

Consider Loss Bonus

Factor in consecutive losses

Assess Enemy Economy

Predict opponent's buy

Make Team Decision

Full buy, force, or save

Common Buy Scenarios

First Round (Pistol)
T Side
  • Nothing (save for second)
  • Armor + Utility
  • Tec-9 + Utility
  • Full Utility Setup
CT Side
  • Nothing (save for second)
  • Armor + Kit
  • Five-Seven + Utility
  • Kit + Full Utility
Force Buy Scenarios
After Pistol Loss
  • Full Save (next round buy)
  • Deagle + Armor
  • SMG + Light Utility
Mid-Game Force
  • Full Save (reset economy)
  • Galil/Famas + Utility
  • Scout + Armor + Utility

Equipment Value Guide

Full Buy
$5,000+
Rifle, armor, full utility, kit (CT)
Force Buy
$2,500-3,500
SMG/cheap rifle, partial utility
Eco
$0-1,500
Save money, minimal investment

Aim Training

Improving Your Aim

Consistent aim training is key to improving your performance in CS2.

Tracking Practice
Duration

10-15 min

Focus

Smooth tracking

  • Follow moving targets
  • Practice different speeds
  • Maintain consistent distance
Flick Training
Duration

15-20 min

Focus

Quick precision

  • Practice snap targeting
  • Various target sizes
  • Different distances
Spray Control
Duration

20 min

Focus

Pattern mastery

  • Learn spray patterns
  • Practice recoil control
  • Moving targets practice
